description:
The map is a FLAT SORTED ARRAY, not a HAMT. Elixir's structural-sharing intuitions do not transfer, and the module's shape must reflect that.

  op        Elixir (HAMT)   fz (flat sorted array)
  get       O(log32 n)      O(n) LINEAR SCAN -- sorted but not binary-searched
                            (runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:806)
  put       O(log32 n)      O(n) full copy
  delete    O(log32 n)      DOES NOT EXIST -- no fz_map_delete anywhere
  merge     O(m log n)      O(n+m) linear merge -- BETTER than Elixir, relatively
  fold acc  O(n log n)      O(n^2)

Today only 3 of the 22 fz_map_* runtime symbols are reachable from fz source
(map.fz:4 -- count, entry_key, entry_value). Map has zero of Elixir's 40-pair API,
and zero fixtures use it by name.

Work:
  - binary search in Heap::read_map_addr_value_ref (the array is already sorted)
  - fz_map_delete
  - a Map module whose FIRST-CLASS surface is bulk and single-pass -- new/1, merge/2,
    take/2, drop/2, filter/2, split/2 -- built through the existing
    fz_map_dest_begin/put/freeze builder, with put/3 and delete/2 documented as the
    slow path callers must not use in loops. That emphasis is the opposite of
    Elixir's docs and must be written down.

Consequence to record: Enum.frequencies, frequencies_by, group_by, uniq, uniq_by and
Map.new are O(n^2) with a map accumulator. Prefer sort-then-group once fz-5xp.8 lands.
title: Map: binary-search lookup, delete primitive, and a bulk-first Map module
